description: Comprehensiveness, sufficiency, deletion AOPC and token-level rationale F1 for the already-computed whole-word POS-NEG margin Partition SHAP values of BERT and CLIP-text on the 500-sentence SST-2 set.

ranking.name: shap_abs
ranking.rule: content words ordered by |phi_margin| descending, ties broken by word position (the source experiment's primary deletion ranking); punctuation units are never ranked or removed

comprehensiveness_sufficiency_scale.name: model_mean_abs_decision_score
comprehensiveness_sufficiency_scale.rule: raw comprehensiveness and sufficiency are divided by S_model = mean over the 500 sentences of |s(x)|, s(x) = d * margin(x); one constant per model

sufficiency_keep_rule: keep the top-k content words and every punctuation unit; delete all other content words with the same whole-word deletion masker

rationale.reference_rule: content word whose SST human sentiment rating is outside the SST neutral interval (0.4, 0.6], i.e. rating <= 0.4 or rating > 0.6
rationale.selection_rule: SHAP-selected words = the same top-k content words (|phi_margin| ranking, k_f = max(1, ceil(f * n_content))) used for comprehensiveness and sufficiency; P/R/F1 per fraction, averaged over the fractions
rationale.empty_reference_rule: sentences with no reference sentiment word are excluded (recall undefined); the reference does not depend on the model, so the excluded sentences are identical for BERT and CLIP
rationale.note: The evaluation CSV has no human rationale annotations. The SST word ratings are human, but context-free: they are a lexical proxy for rationales, not rationales for each sentence's label.
